notes: Thunderbird for Android (formerly K-9 Mail) on Google Play as net.thunderbird.android, MZLA-funded with in-house design. This import RETARGETS: it was written against :feature:account:setup of the root build, and a checkout says that cannot work. Every preview in the root build lives in a src/debug source set — 116 files of them — and the preview plugin discovers the MAIN source set only, which is the same reason Confetti's screenshotTest previews were dropped from its spec. The design system is the right target anyway: components/ is an included build (rootProject.name = "components", its own settings.gradle.kts) whose :ui:bolt module holds 102 files declaring 288 @Preview functions in commonMain, organised atom / molecule / organism / template. It was unreachable from here until workingDirectory existed; naming components as the Gradle root is exactly what that field is for, and this is its second user after mullvad. Bolt is a KMP Compose module with an Android target and pulls in compose.ui.tooling deliberately "to enable Android Studio Composable preview", so it renders on the Robolectric lane. previewAnnotations names the four multipreviews its previews carry — @PreviewLightDark from AndroidX plus Bolt's own @PreviewDevices, @PreviewDevicesWithBackground and @PreviewLightDarkLandscape — without which discovery sees 232 of the 288. The inventory catalogues 252 of them: 36 previews are declared under a name Bolt reuses across files — 32 called simply `Preview` and four `IconPreview` — and a spec entry naming one would fold every same-named preview into a single sticker, which the pre-flight warns about. They stay out. The render reaches 357 of 364 previews; excludePreviewIds names the other seven. Six read Bolt's `ThemeSizes` CompositionLocal without providing it — the two BadgeIcon previews (four with @PreviewLightDark) and the `Preview` functions in FilledNewMailBadge.kt and FilledUnreadMailBadge.kt — and die with `IllegalStateException: No ThemeSizes provided`. They render in Android Studio because its preview host supplies the theme; standalone there is nothing to supply it, and the fix would be upstream's to make (wrap each in the theme, as Bolt's other previews do). The seventh, RemoteImagePreview, resolves a coil3 network fetcher (`ClassNotFoundException: coil3.network.ktor3.KtorNetworkFetcher`) that the render classpath has no reason to carry. The three of the seven that the inventory catalogued are dropped from it with them, so the spec and the render agree. The spec declares breakpoints for Bolt's six @PreviewDevices widths (360, 411, 673, 891, 1280, 1920): without them the join maps every render to the generic Material width class, and five components — list-detail-pane, responsive-content, responsive-content-with-background, responsive-width-container and scaffold, each annotated @PreviewDevices with no theme axis to separate them — collapse three devices onto size=expanded and fail the join with "produces duplicate output axes". The schema names this case exactly. Naming the widths gives each device its own axis, which is also the sticker sheet a responsive template should have. Apache-2.0.
